meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 10: Debugging (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: A stdio server is producing parse errors at the client. Which causes are plausible? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The client sent two requests before reading the first response
A JSON message contains an embedded newline
A log line is emitted with print() instead of to stderr
A library writes a progress bar to stdout
The server writes its responses to stderr instead of stdout

questions.explanation: stdout is protocol-only and messages are newline-delimited with no embedded newlines, so A, B and C corrupt framing. Writing responses to stderr produces silence, not parse errors, and interleaved requests are normal: correlation is by id.

questions.question: A tool call fails in the host and you do not yet know whose fault it is. Which steps actually narrow that down? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Re-publish the server to the registry to refresh its metadata
Run the same call through the Inspector CLI against the same server
Compare the protocol version each side advertises
Delete the client's cache directory and reconnect
Read the server's stderr log, which the host captures separately

questions.explanation: A second client, the server's own error stream and the advertised revisions each isolate a different layer: server logic, server runtime and version negotiation. Clearing caches and re-publishing change nothing about a failing call.

questions.question: Which client-visible outcomes point at a header or metadata problem rather than a tool bug? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: 400 with -32020 after a gateway rewrote Mcp-Name
200 with isError: true after the tool's upstream API failed
404 with -32601 after calling a method the server does not implement
400 with -32022 listing the server's supported versions

questions.explanation: A, B and C are all metadata or header validation failures, and all are 400. A tool result with isError is a business failure, and -32601 means the method itself is unknown, not that its metadata was wrong.
